newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOCCER-SWEDEN SURVIVE LATE ESTONIAN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN SURVIVE LATE ESTONIAN CHARGE.

text.p: Sweden survived a late bout of pressure to beat Estonia 3-2 in their World Cup European zone group four qualifier on Sunday.
Martin Dahlin fired the Swedes ahead in the 13th minute but a handful of chances went begging before Par Zetterberg converted a 53rd minute penalty.
Estonia hit two late goals after Kennet Andersson's volley had put Sweden 3-0 in front in the 73rd minute.
Midfielder Andres Oper scored from close range after 75 minutes then striker Marko Kristal added another five minutes from time.
Sweden retained third place in the group and have 12 points from six games, Austria are on 13 from six and Scotland have 17 points from eight matches.
Dahlin, of Borussia Moenchengladbach, received a ball knocked down during a scramble in the Estonian box and slipped it past Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom for the opening goal.
From that point, Poom, who plays for English premier league side Derby, had to work hard.
In the 26th minute, Zetterberg shot over the bar after another scramble in the box while Hakan Mild had a chance three minutes later as he headed over the net.

Off-target shots and Poom's efforts managed to frustrate the Swedes for the rest of the first half. They were forced to wait until the eighth minute of the second half before Zetterberg, brought down in the box, converted a penalty.
Andersson seemed to seal an easy victory for the Swedes when he received a ball onto his chest just metres away from the goal and volleyed it past Poom.
But the Estonians fought back in the final minutes, taking advantage of what seemed to be a tired Swedish team.
Oper got behind the Swedish defence as he received a cross from the left wing, firing it past Swedish goalkeeper Magnus Hedman in the 75th minute.
With renewed vigour, Estonia kept the pressure on, hoping to humiliate their more distinguished visitors.
Kristal shocked the Swedes again in the 85th when he fired a hard shot straight past Hedman for Estonia's second.

Estonia - 1-Mart Poom, 2-Marek Lemsalu, 3-Urmas Kirs, 4-Sergei Hohlov-Simson, 5-Janek Meet, 6-Liivo Leetma (18-Kristen Viikmae 45), 7-Meelis Rooba (14-Mati Pari 66), 8-Andres Oper, 9-Marko Kristal, 10-Martin Reim, 11-Indrek Zelinksi.

Sweden: 1-Magnus Hedman, 2-Roland Nilsson, 3-Patrik Andersson, 4-Joachim Bjorklund, 5-Gary Sundgren, 6-Hakan Mild (Niclas Alexandersson 73), 7-Par Zetterberg, 8-Andreas Andersson, 9-Jonas Thern, 10-Martin Dahlin (20-Joergen Pettersson), 11-Kennet Andersson (15-Andreas Jacobsson 85).
